name: SX1278IMLTRT
title: SX1276/77/78/79: 137 MHz to 1020 MHz LoRa and FSK/OOK long-range transceivers
summary: A family of half-duplex sub-GHz radio transceiver chips with two modems: the LoRa spread-spectrum modem and a conventional FSK, GFSK, MSK, GMSK and OOK modem with packet engine. The four parts share one 6 x 6 mm QFN-28 and one register map and differ in frequency coverage and spreading factors; the SX1278 covers only the two low bands (137-175 MHz and 410-525 MHz) and uses SF6 to SF12. A host controls everything over SPI, with six DIO pins for interrupts. Output reaches +14 dBm on the high-efficiency RFO pins and +20 dBm on PA_BOOST; LoRa sensitivity reaches -148 dBm.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 3.7 V (2.4 V to 3.7 V for +20 dBm)
-148 dBm typ, SF12, 7.8 kHz, Band 2 or 3
+20 dBm on PA_BOOST (1 % duty cycle), +17 dBm continuous, +14 dBm on RFO
9.9 mA typ, LoRa, Band 1, BW 7.8-62.5 kHz; 11.0 mA typ in Bands 2&3
120 mA typ at +20 dBm, 87 mA at +17 dBm, 29 mA at +13 dBm on RFO
FSK 1.2-300 kbps; OOK 1.2-32.768 kbps; LoRa 0.018-37.5 kbps
QFN-28, 6 x 6 mm, 0.65 mm pitch, -40 °C to +85 °C

Its output drives XTA directly, XTB is left unconnected, and the TCXO supply carries a decoupling capacitor CD whose value comes from the TCXO maker. TcxoInputOn in RegTcxo is set to 1, and the clock at XTA stays at or below 1.8 V peak-to-peak.

operation.text: All four parts share the die features and package. SX1276 and SX1279 run SF6 to SF12 in every band they cover; SX1277 is limited to SF6 to SF9; SX1278 keeps SF6 to SF12 and bandwidths of 7.8 to 500 kHz but only reaches the lower UHF bands, so its pins 21 and 22 are grounds.

A half-duplex low-IF receiver: single-ended LNA inputs, conversion to differential, an I/Q mixer, two sigma-delta converters, and all filtering and demodulation done digitally. Two fractional-N synthesizers make the LO, one for the low bands up to 525 MHz and one for the high band from 779 MHz. FSK is modulated inside the PLL loop, with optional Gaussian pre-filtering. Timing comes from a 32 MHz crystal oscillator and a low-power RC oscillator.

Three PAs. PA_LF (on RFO_LF) and PA_HF (on RFO_HF) are unregulated, efficient, and adjust from -4 to +14 dBm in 1 dB steps into 50 Ω; their output follows the supply and is specified at 3.3 V. Each can share an antenna port with its receiver input through two passive parts. PA_HP on PA_BOOST is regulated, covers all bands, runs continuously to +17 dBm and duty-cycled to +20 dBm through its own matching network.

Writing 0x87 to RegPaDac lifts PA_BOOST to +20 dBm; it must be returned to 0x84 when an RFO PA is used. At +20 dBm the supply must be 2.4 V to 3.7 V, transmit duty cycle at most 1 % and antenna VSWR at most 3:1 over -40 °C to +85 °C. The OCP limit in RegOcp should be raised to match the power level.

A current limiter on the PAs guards against bad RF loads and caps peak battery draw. OcpTrim sets the limit from 45 mA to 240 mA, 100 mA by default; it covers the PA alone, so total chip current can reach Imax plus IDDFS.

Supply enters on VBAT_ANA, VBAT_RF and VBAT_DIG from any low-noise source. Internal regulators keep characteristics steady over temperature and supply: +17 dBm is held across a 1.8 V to 3.7 V supply, while +20 dBm needs at least 2.4 V. VR_PA, VR_DIG and VR_ANA each need a decoupling capacitor for their regulators.
An interrupt fires when the supply falls below a threshold set in RegLowBat (1.695 V to 2.185 V in eight steps); it can be routed to a DIO pin.

A Pierce oscillator on XTA and XTB with a 32 MHz crystal is the reference for the synthesizers and all digital logic. Start-up time depends on the crystal; the PLL starts automatically once the oscillator is stable. Load capacitors (10 to 22 pF foot capacitance per pin) are fitted externally to suit the crystal's specified load.

A TCXO can replace the crystal: set TcxoInputOn in RegTcxo, feed the clock into XTA and leave XTB open. The input must never exceed 1.8 V peak-to-peak. For LoRa bandwidths below 62.5 kHz a TCXO is advised to stay within the frequency-error tolerance.

DIO5 can output the reference clock or FXOSC divided by 2 to 32 (ClkOut in RegOsc), in every mode but Sleep; it is on after power-on reset. It can clock a host or be measured to trim crystal tolerance in software, and should be turned off when not needed to save current.

Both PLLs use a 19-bit sigma-delta modulator, giving a constant 61 Hz step. The 24-bit Frf value is spread over 0x06 to 0x08 and only takes effect when the low byte is written; with FastHopOn the write to RegFrfLsb changes frequency immediately, which also lets the host build slow multi-level FSK. Each PLL has four selectable loop bandwidths (75 to 300 kHz).
A low-power RC oscillator (62.5 kHz after calibration) times the sequencer while in Sleep; it is calibrated at power-up without user action.
A POR runs at power-up. After VDD is applied, wait 10 ms from the end of the POR before using SPI, and keep NRESET floating during POR. Activity on CLKOUT also shows the chip is ready.
Drive NRESET low for about 100 us and release it, then wait 5 ms before using the chip. While NRESET is held low, VDD current can rise by up to 1 mA.

Slave-only SPI, CPOL = 0 and CPHA = 0, up to 10 MHz. Each frame starts with NSS low and an address byte: a write/read bit (1 = write) then a 7-bit address, MSB first, followed by data MSB first. Single access moves one byte; burst access auto-increments the address; addressing the FIFO keeps the same address for every byte. MOSI is sampled on rising SCK and MISO changes on falling SCK; MISO floats while NSS is high. During a write, MISO returns the register's previous value.

The LoRa modem replaces the FSK modem through RegOpMode, a change allowed only in Sleep, so a design can use both. Three settings trade link budget, interference immunity, occupied spectrum and data rate: spreading factor, bandwidth and coding rate. The register map changes in LoRa mode; LoRa configuration is kept while in FSK mode. Configuration registers are readable in every mode; writes belong in Sleep or Standby. The top-level sequencer does not work in LoRa mode.

Each symbol is spread over 2^SF chips (64 to 4096). Transmitter and receiver must use the same SF, since different SFs are orthogonal and can share a channel. Higher SF lets the receiver work at more negative SNR, down to -20 dB at SF12.

SF6 gives the highest LoRa data rate and needs special settings: SpreadingFactor = 6, implicit header mode, DetectionOptimize = 0b101 in RegDetectOptimize and 0x0C in RegDetectionThreshold. These go back to defaults for other SFs.

Cyclic forward error correction at 4/5 to 4/8 adds 1.25x to 2x overhead. In explicit header mode (the default) a short header carries payload length, coding rate and CRC presence, sent at 4/8 with its own CRC. In implicit mode the header is dropped, saving air time, and both ends must be configured with the same length, rate and CRC setting; SF6 works only in implicit mode.

In explicit mode only the transmitter's RxPayloadCrcOn decides whether a CRC is sent; the receiver reads CrcOnPayload in RegHopChannel and, if set, checks PayloadCrcError. In implicit mode RxPayloadCrcOn must be set on both ends.

Default preamble is 12 symbols. PreambleLength can be set from 6 to 65535, giving 6+4 to 65535+4 symbols. The receiver should use the same length as the transmitter, or the maximum if the length is unknown, because preamble search restarts periodically.
LowDataRateOptimize makes long-symbol links tolerant of frequency drift during a packet. It is required when the symbol time exceeds 16 ms and must match on both ends.

LoRa bandwidth is double-sided (whole channel), unlike FSK bandwidth which is single-sided. Wider bandwidth raises data rate and costs sensitivity; 250 and 500 kHz are not supported in the 169 MHz band.

A 256-byte RAM buffer, reachable only in LoRa mode and not in Sleep, holds both Tx and Rx data. RegFifoTxBaseAddr (default 0x80) and RegFifoRxBaseAddr (default 0x00) split it; either can be anywhere, or both at 0x00 to use the whole buffer for one direction. RegFifoAddrPtr sets the SPI access point and auto-increments. The buffer clears on entering Sleep, keeps data across other modes, and is written in Rx even when the CRC fails; an oversized received packet overwrites the Tx area.

RegIrqFlagsMask masks interrupts (1 = masked; all enabled by default). RegIrqFlags shows which fired; a flag clears when 1 is written to it. Six DIO pins carry selected interrupts according to RegDioMapping1 and RegDioMapping2.

Configure in Sleep, Standby or FSTX; fill the FIFO in Standby by pointing FifoAddrPtr to FifoTxBaseAddr and writing PayloadLength bytes; request TX. RF, PLL and PA run only for the packet. TxDone fires at the end and the chip returns to Standby.

RXSINGLE searches for a preamble for a window of RegSymbTimeout symbols (4 to 1023). With no preamble, RxTimeout fires and the chip goes to Standby. After a valid header (ValidHeader in explicit mode) the packet is received, RxDone fires with PayloadCrcError if the CRC is bad, and the chip returns to Standby. The timeout does not fire while a packet is being received, so the host can sleep and rely on the radio's own timer.

RXCONTINUOUS scans for preambles without end, receiving packet after packet and raising RxDone for each; it never times out or returns to Standby on its own. Packets are written back to back, the Rx pointer is never reset, and the host must manage the buffer and read status before the next RxDone. An over-long preamble is silently dropped and the search restarts.
After RxDone with no error flags, set RegFifoAddrPtr to RegFifoRxCurrentAddr and read RegFifo RegRxNbBytes times. Alternatively start from RegFifoRxByteAddr minus RegRxNbBytes.

LoRa has no hardware address filter. The host can latch RegFifoRxByteAddr at each RxDone as the next packet's start, then after ValidHeader poll it until the first address bytes have arrived, check them, and drop to Sleep if the packet is for another node.

CAD looks for a LoRa preamble with minimum energy: the PLL locks, the receiver captures about one symbol at full Rx current, then turns off while the modem correlates the samples at reduced current. CadDone fires at the end, with CadDetected if a preamble was found, and the chip returns to Standby; the host then starts RXSINGLE or RXCONTINUOUS. CAD takes roughly 1.75 to 2.25 symbol periods depending on SF.

With FreqHoppingPeriod non-zero, the packet is split across channels from a host-held frequency list, each dwell lasting a whole number of symbols. Preamble and header go on channel 0. At each hop FhssPresentChannel increments and FhssChangeChannel fires; the host writes the next frequency within the hop period and clears the flag. Reception starts on channel 0 after preamble detection and falls back to channel 0 on a header CRC error.

In LoRa receive the modem measures the offset of the incoming signal, reliable over ±25 % of bandwidth, as a signed 20-bit FreqError in the RegFei registers. Correction is done by the host: subtract the error from the RF frequency, then write 0.95 times the ppm offset into register 0x27 to correct the data rate.
RegModemStat bits help debugging in Rx: bit 0 a preamble is detected, bit 1 the modem has synchronized at the end of preamble, bit 3 a header with valid CRC was received.

Bit rate derives from the crystal through a 16-bit divider plus a 4-bit fraction for 250 ppm resolution; the fraction is ignored in OOK. In continuous transmit, data on DIO2/DATA goes straight to the modulator, asynchronously unless Gaussian shaping is on, in which case DCLK on DIO1 paces the data.

FSK alters the PLL fractional divider; deviation can be very narrow and must lie between 600 Hz and 200 kHz with FDEV + BR/2 at most 250 kHz. OOK switches the PA on and off with optional ramping. Gaussian BT 0.5 or 1 shaping (FSK) or PA bias ramping (OOK) narrows the spectrum; changing ModulationShaping requires restarting the transmitter.

Compares RSSI against a threshold: peak (recommended), fixed, or average (only for DC-free data). In peak mode the threshold sits 6 dB under the RSSI peak and decays by OokPeakThreshStep every OokPeakThreshDec down to the floor set by OokFixedThresh. The floor is tuned per design by raising OokFixedThresh, with no input in continuous mode, until DATA stops glitching.

Recovers clean data and clock from received edges, on DIO2/DATA and DIO1/DCLK in continuous mode; always on in packet mode and advised in continuous mode. It needs a preamble of at least 12 bits of 0x55 or 0xAA, an edge at least every 16 bits, and a bit-rate error under 6.5 %.

The FEI measures carrier offset in 4 bit periods during the preamble, provided offset plus 20 dB signal bandwidth fits in the filter. AFC subtracts the result from Frf each time the receiver starts if AfcAutoOn = 1; AfcAutoClearOn picks whether to start each correction from the original frequency. RegAfcBw sets a wider filter for the AFC phase. The PreambleDetect flag can gate AFC so it runs only on a valid preamble.
Flags a 0101 pattern regardless of frequency offset within the filter; size 1 to 3 bytes, normally 2 bytes with PreambleDetectTol = 10. It can gate AGC and AFC.

Image rejection is 35 dB uncalibrated and about 48 dB after calibration of I/Q phase and gain. Calibration runs at POR and manual reset (low band only, at 434 MHz), on a temperature change of 5 to 20 °C if enabled, or on demand via ImageCalStart in Standby. It takes about 10 ms and needs the chip in FSK/OOK mode. It should be repeated at the working frequency, and disabling the automatic temperature-triggered run avoids unexpected packet loss.
Three timeouts can shut the receiver down if RSSI, preamble or sync address does not appear in time, each set in units of 16 bit periods and enabled through RxTrigger in RegRxConfig.

From Sleep the chip passes through Standby (TS_OSC), the synthesizer (TS_FS) and then Tx (TS_TR) or Rx (TS_RE). TS_RE depends only on the receiver bandwidth (RxBwAfc with AFC on), from 63 us at 250 kHz to 2.33 ms at 2.6 kHz. The first RSSI sample follows TS_RSSI later. Tx-Rx and Rx-Tx turnaround take TS_HOP plus TS_RE or TS_TR. For fast Rx hopping, set FastHopOn and write the new Frf, then wait TS_HOP.

operation.topic: AGC and AFC at receiver start
operation.text: AGC and AFC run per packet when the receiver turns on, on a user restart (RestartRxWithoutPllLock, or RestartRxWithPllLock when AFC is on or Frf changed), or on automatic restart. AutoRestartRxMode restarts after the host empties the FIFO, waiting InterPacketRxDelay, with an extra PLL lock delay if the frequency changed. With RestartRxOnCollision the receiver restarts on a sudden RSSI rise, threshold in 1 dB steps.

In FSK/OOK the AGC handles signals from sensitivity up to 0 dBm or more by stepping through six LNA gains (G1 to G6) at thresholds AgcThresh1 to 5, trading noise figure for linearity. With AgcAutoOn = 0 the gain is fixed by LnaGain. LnaBoostHf = 11 raises HF LNA current to 150 %.

RSSI is measured inside the receiver bandwidth with 0.5 dB resolution; RssiOffset corrects for matching loss or an external LNA in 1 dB steps. Averaging over 2 to 256 samples (RssiSmoothing) trades response time against accuracy (±6 dB to ±1.1 dB at 10 dB SNR).

LoRa RSSI uses a -157 offset on the HF port and -164 on the LF port; packets below the noise floor add PacketSnr/4. PacketRssi is averaged; above about -100 dBm it loses linearity, where sampling Rssi during the payload or the 16/15 slope correction helps. The offsets change with LNA boost, external LNA or mismatch and can be trimmed by a one-point calibration.
A 16-tap FIR filter sets the single-side FSK bandwidth from 2.6 to 250 kHz. Adjacent channel rejection is limited by LO phase noise, not the filter. Bit rate must stay below twice RxBw.

Measures in every mode except Sleep and Standby; absolute accuracy is ±10 °C, improved by calibrating at one known temperature. Reading sequence: Standby and wait for the oscillator, FSRx, TempMonitorOff = 0, wait 140 us, TempMonitorOff = 1, back to Sleep or Standby, read RegTemp. TempValue counts -1 °C per LSB and wraps through 0 near 15 to 25 °C on a typical device.
RegOpMode selects Sleep, Standby, FSTx, Tx, FSRx or Rx by hand; blocks wake in a fixed optimized order on each change. The top-level sequencer can automate mode changes in FSK/OOK only.

A programmable state machine, FSK/OOK only, moves between Idle, Transmit, Receive, PacketReceived, LowPowerSelection and RxTimeout states on interrupts and two timers (64 us, 4.1 ms or 262 ms resolution times a coefficient). Start it with SequencerStart in Sleep or Standby; Stop forces it off at any time; the two bits must never be set together. Both timers must run for periodic cycling.

Using the sequencer, the chip idles in Sleep with the RC oscillator and wakes every T1 + T2 to receive for up to T2. Waking on PreambleDetect needs a preamble lasting T1 + 2 × T2. Waking on SyncAddress sets T1 to 64 us, sizes a short RxTimeout to catch a preamble, and makes the preamble T2 minus the sync time.

With BeaconOn set and a fixed-length payload shorter than the FIFO, the FIFO content is restored after each transmission, so the sequencer can resend the same packet every T1 + T2 with no host action. Exit by clearing BeaconOn and setting FifoOverrun.

Continuous mode puts each bit on DIO2/DATA in real time with DCLK on DIO1; packet mode (recommended) uses the 64-byte FIFO and packet handler for preamble, sync word, CRC, DC-free coding and address filtering, with payloads up to 255, 2047 bytes or unlimited.

64 bytes, MSB first through an 8-bit shift register. Flags: FifoEmpty, FifoFull, FifoOverrunFlag (clears the FIFO when written 1), PacketSent and FifoLevel against FifoThreshold. Entering Rx or leaving Tx clears it; Standby and Sleep keep it.

Sync word recognition, 1 to 8 bytes, compares incoming bits with SyncValue starting from bit 7 of RegSyncValue1, and is reused to generate the sync word in Tx. Values containing a 0x00 byte are not allowed.

Fixed length (PacketFormat = 0, PayloadLength > 0): payload up to 2047 bytes, at least 1. Variable length (PacketFormat = 1): a length byte first, payload up to 255 bytes. Unlimited (PacketFormat = 0, PayloadLength = 0): no length counting, no Rx CRC check, CrcOk and PayloadReady unavailable. Each packet is preamble (0 to 65535 bytes), sync word (0 to 8 bytes), optional length and address bytes, message and optional 2-byte CRC.

In Tx the handler adds preamble and sync word, optional CRC and DC-free coding; it starts when TxStartCondition is met (first byte in FIFO, or FifoThreshold + 1 bytes) and sends preamble while waiting. In Rx it strips preamble and sync word, decodes, checks address and CRC, and raises PayloadReady on DIO0. A failed CRC clears the FIFO and suppresses PayloadReady unless CrcAutoClearOff = 1. Packets larger than 64 bytes are streamed using FifoThreshold, FifoEmpty and FifoFull.

AddressFiltering = 01 matches NodeAddress; 10 matches NodeAddress or BroadcastAddress; the address byte stays in the FIFO and applies to Rx only. In variable length mode PayloadLength is the maximum accepted length; 2047 disables the check.

Manchester (DcFree = 01) codes 1 as 10 and 0 as 01, halving the actual bit rate, and covers payload and CRC only. Whitening (DcFree = 10) XORs payload and CRC with a 9-bit LFSR sequence (X9 + X5 + 1) and keeps the bit rate. Only one can be active.
An io-homecontrol compatibility mode exists; details come from Semtech on request.
The exposed pad's land should carry thermal vias to a system ground plane for thermal and electrical performance.
